articles.title: NASH Group Highlights India's Manufacturing and Edge AI Capabilities at electronica 2026
articles.content: Capabilities of NASH Group in engineering, electronics production, and embedded systems will be exhibited at the electronica 2026 event. The event will be held from 10 to 13 November 2026 at the Messe München in Munich, Germany, where the firm will host visitors at stand A6.466. During the trade show, NASH Group will showcase its end-to-end skills in various key service areas: ODM – Original Design Manufacturing: Involving all the phases of product development cycle, from prototyping and localization to mass production. EMS – Electronics Manufacturing Services: Supplying key manufacturing services like PCB assembly and custom wire harnesses. Mechanical & Box-Build Assembly: Providing sheet metal fabrication, machining, box build assembly and system integration. Embedded & AI Technologies: Developing dedicated hardware and software, AIoT solutions, Smart Vision solutions and edge AI technologies. Through the integration of engineering, software, mechanical, wiring, assembly, and testing services, the NASH Group provides a vertically integrated service. This enables clients around the world to have a more streamlined process by working with one vendor from the conceptualization stage right up until production. Key Technology Highlights The company’s exhibition will showcase several high-tech innovations and hardware solutions: The Land of Robots Meets ENCY 3.0: ENCY World in Seoul Also Read Industrial Computing: Features what the company notes as India’s first industrial motherboard, alongside industrial Box PCs and single-board computers built for rugged applications. Smart Vision & Edge AI: Demonstrations of an AI vision camera and intelligent edge computing technologies designed for industrial automation. Energy Storage & Battery Management Solutions: Presentation of hardware along with Smart Battery Management Systems (BMS). Examples of these BMS include Battmonx, BMS Automation, and EVolt. These BMS work on LFP battery chemistry as well as NMC battery chemistry. They serve in electric mobility, renewable energy storage systems, UPS systems, and telecom applications. Leadership Outlook Arun Bhat, President of NASH Industries, noted that electronica serves as a critical global platform for the electronics sector. He emphasized that NASH Group’s participation highlights how the company brings together product design, embedded systems, intelligent vision, energy management, and advanced manufacturing in India to support international clients and scale complex products efficiently. TME highlights the Arduino VENTUNO Q at electronica Also Read Global Network and Operations With over five decades of collective manufacturing experience, NASH Group brings together three key business arms: NASH Industries, NASH Tech Labs, and NASH Energy. Manufacturing Infrastructure: Operates more than 15 production facilities located across India (including major hubs in Bengaluru, Chennai, and Pune) as well as Dubai. Global Presence: Maintains dedicated international sales offices in Europe, the United States, and Japan, backed by a warehouse facility in the US. Research & Scale: Employs over 175 dedicated R&D engineers and exports products to more than 25 countries worldwide. articles.title: Hyderabad startup opens space debris removal facility - The New Indian Express
articles.content: HYDERABAD: Hyderabad-based spacetech startup Cosmoserve Space on Thursday inaugurated India’s first private facility for developing and testing technologies to capture defunct satellites, remove space debris and service spacecraft in orbit. Named Base 1, the facility is the sixth of its kind globally, according to the company. Inaugurated by Minister of State for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh and IT Minister D Sridhar Babu, the facility brings together infrastructure for designing, building and testing satellite servicing systems. It houses an Orbital Rendezvous and Capture Lab, a Space Robotics Innovation Lab, an ISO Class 8 clean room and a Mission Simulation and Control Centre. The infrastructure will support the development of robotic systems to capture defunct satellites, as well as technologies for in-orbit repairs and refuelling. Sridhar Babu said the state government planned to introduce a Space Technology Policy within a year. Hyderabad was home to more than 30 spacetech companies working in areas such as launch vehicles, space data centres and debris removal. He also announced that space technology would be the 34th sector covered by the industry-led Young India Skills University. Cosmoserve is developing a dual-spacecraft system in which a larger orbital station will serve as a refuelling and logistics hub, while smaller autonomous vehicles will capture, inspect, repair or remove satellites. The company aims to begin commercial debris removal operations by early 2028, after technology demonstration missions. The need for such services is growing as defunct satellites and fragments crowd Earth’s orbit, threatening operational spacecraft and future launches. Cosmoserve estimates that nearly 10,000 of the approximately 28,000 satellites in orbit are non-operational. Its technology is being designed to handle debris ranging from 10 cm fragments to satellites weighing up to 500 kg. “What is the point of building bigger rockets and developing capabilities to colonise the Moon and Mars if we cannot even cross our orbits?” said founder and CEO Chiranjeevi Phanindra. articles.title: Dhinidhi Desinghu wins India's first Youth Olympic swimming bronze - The News Mill
articles.content: ANI Photo | Dhinidhi Desinghu wins India’s first Youth Olympic swimming bronze Dhinidhi Desinghu, aged 16, created history by winning India’s first-ever swimming medal at the Youth Olympic Games 2026 held in Dakar, Senegal. The Bengaluru swimmer secured a bronze in the women’s 100m freestyle event on Monday, setting a new national record with a time of 56.27 seconds. Desinghu finished behind Croatia’s Ana Bobanović, who claimed gold in 55.89 seconds, and New Zealand’s Alyssa Lawson, who took silver in 56.13 seconds. This also marked India’s first medal at the current edition of the Youth Olympic Games. ADVERTISEMENT Stay connected Make The News Mill your preferred source See more TNM stories when you search for news on Google. Add TNM on Google Desinghu is the first Indian female swimmer to reach a Youth Olympic Games final and subsequently earn a podium finish. Remarkably, her journey began with a fear of water. As a young child, she was so scared of entering a pool that she once ran back home in her swimsuit rather than swim. “I know I was really scared,” Desinghu told Olympics.com after her medal-winning performance. “There’s a story from when I was six or seven… We went to the pool during summer break… I went to the pool and then ran back home in my swimsuit because I just hated being there,” she said. ADVERTISEMENT Her parents had to enter the pool themselves to encourage her to learn swimming. What started as a convenient activity due to their proximity to the pool gradually transformed into a passion and a competitive pursuit. “I’m not really sure how I fell in love with swimming, but as the years went by, I grew to love it,” she added. At 14, Desinghu was the youngest member of India’s contingent at the Paris 2024 Olympics, where she competed alongside some of the world’s leading swimmers, including French athlete Leon Marchand. She described the experience of sharing the Olympic Village and competing in the same pool as swimmers she had only previously watched on television as unforgettable. At Dakar, Desinghu qualified for the 100m freestyle final with the third-fastest overall time of 56.80 seconds in the heats. She improved her time by 0.53 seconds in the final to secure the bronze medal and set a national record. ADVERTISEMENT “I wasn’t really thinking about a medal. It was mostly about improving my time,” she said. Bajaj Finserv, which began supporting Desinghu earlier this year as part of its commitment to nurturing young sporting talent in India, acknowledged her achievement. Manav Mianwal, Group Chief Marketing Officer of Bajaj Finserv Ltd and President – Digital Platforms at Bajaj Finance Ltd, commented: “Dhinidhi’s historic bronze is a proud moment for India and an inspiration for every young athlete who dares to dream big. Behind this medal are years of hard work, sacrifice and extraordinary determination. Her achievement shows that Indian talent can compete with the best in the world when individual talent is matched with collective support.”...

articles.title: Dr Jitendra inaugurates Hyderabad facility developed by India's first ' Space Debris Removal' StartUp
articles.content: NEW DELHI, Nov 5: India is emerging among the early global pioneers in Space debris removal, with an Indian StartUp advancing technologies to make outer space safer and more sustainable, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh said today. Announcing a vision of achieving debris-free Space by 2030, the Minister said India's emerging capabilities in active space debris removal reflect the country's growing global leadership in space technology and its commitment to ensuring a safe space environment for the entire humanity. Dr. Jitendra Singh was speaking virtually from Kartavya Bhawan, New Delhi, at the inauguration of Cosmoserve Space's Base 1 facility in Hyderabad. The inauguration ceremony at VSD Tech Park, Gachibowli, Hyderabad, was attended by D. Sridhar Babu, Minister for IT and Industries, Government of Telangana, as Guest of Honour, and Dr Chiranjeevi Phanindra, Founder and CEO, Cosmoserve Space. Dr. Jitendra Singh joined the programme virtually as Chief Guest. Congratulating Cosmoserve Space on the inauguration, Dr. Jitendra Singh said Base 1 is a comprehensive, state-of-the-art facility spread across approximately 14,800 square feet, where space robots are designed, built, tested under space conditions and operated through mission control. The facility houses specialised capabilities including orbital rendezvous and capture labs, space robotics innovation labs, microgravity simulation platforms and satellite integration clean rooms, marking a significant advancement in India's private space capabilities. The Minister congratulated Dr. Chiranjeevi Phanindra and his team for pioneering work in active debris removal (ADR) and in-orbit servicing. Mission EMBRACE, which conducted an in-space test of soft robotic petals in July 2026 within a year of the company's formation, reflects the rapid progress and growing technological maturity of India's private space startups. He appreciated the team's experience in ISRO and the Gaganyaan programme being translated into a collaborative model in the private sector. Dr. Jitendra Singh said Cosmoserve Space's partnerships with Pixxel for satellite systems, Dhruv Aerospace for propulsion systems and Skyroot Aerospace for launch services demonstrate an emerging culture of end-to-end collaboration in space technology. The initiative showcases how Indian startups are combining indigenous payloads, battery technologies, satellite systems and private launch capabilities to build integrated space missions and establish global benchmarks. The Minister said India never lacked scientific talent or technological capabilities; what was needed was an enabling ecosystem to unlock the immense potential of its youth. He called upon domestic and international investors to participate more actively in the space sector and urged greater philanthropy in science and research to accelerate innovation, strengthen collaborations and support emerging technologies. Dr. Jitendra Singh said India's ultimate objective remains technological self-reliance and sovereign capabilities, alongside international partnerships. India's achievements in Chandrayaan and the Gaganyaan programme demonstrate its ability to undertake sophisticated missions at significantly lower costs. He also emphasised that India's space capabilities are transforming life on Earth through applications in Gati Shakti, smart cities, disaster preparedness and several other areas directly benefiting citizens.
